sourcePolicy: Process language is limited to the written service terms already published on the website. Case proof must use named public work with a current source, or an existing case-study fact. Google review excerpts are never assigned to a client unless the review record names that client.

process.heading: See it first. Price it clearly. Build it together.
process.intro: Start with the public customer path. Paid work starts only after the written scope makes the work clear.

steps.title: First look
steps.body: Show us the business and what needs to work better. We look at the public path and name the useful next move.

steps.title: Written scope and price
steps.body: Before paid work starts, you get the scope, exact price, responsibilities, review rounds, launch timing, and support terms in writing.

steps.title: Build, review, launch
steps.body: We build the agreed work. You review the working pages and customer path before launch.

items.summary: A Phoenix customer can recognize the work, find the relevant service, and start a project conversation without a generic contractor maze.
A new client can book without a DM detour. The site explains Rachel’s work, then hands off to the booking tool clients already know.
